title: Postcard and Promise
premise: Lior Ishikawa, a celebrated wedding planner who abandoned belief in marriage after her own engagement collapsed, is court-ordered into a community reconciliation program that pairs anonymous pen-pals to write honestly about their worst mistakes. Her assigned correspondent turns out to be Daniel Voss, the rival event magnate whose company destroyed her career — and neither knows it at first, because they write under pseudonyms. As their letters deepen into love, Lior is simultaneously hired to plan the merger celebration that will seal Daniel's takeover of her former firm, forcing her to choose between the revenge she's rehearsed for years and the man on the page. When identities are revealed mid-ceremony, betrayal and forgiveness collide; in the end, Lior must forgive herself for surviving her own broken promise, and she and Daniel marry not as planners of a perfect day but as two people who finally stopped performing one.
about_author: Kestrel Marchetti is a former hospitality insider who spent a decade orchestrating other people's happiest days before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal apartment cluttered with unsent postcards, exploring how love survives the stories we tell about ourselves.

chapters.title: The Muscle Theory
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She runs a flawless wedding while privately reciting her creed: the heart is trainable, containable. A panic attack in the coat room reveals the cost of control. Emotional beat: polished surface, cracking foundation.

chapters.title: Court Date, White Dress
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. After a public confrontation with rival Daniel Voss at an industry gala, a judge sentences them both to the Bridge Letters program — anonymous correspondence with a stranger about their worst failure. Beat: humiliation disguised as justice.

chapters.title: Dear Stranger
chapters.summary: Alternating letters. Under pseudonyms 'Postcard' (Lior) and 'Anchor' (Daniel), each writes a sanitized half-truth about their past. The first real honesty slips out accidentally. Beat: guarded curiosity, first spark.

chapters.title: The Merger Memo
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. His company acquires Lior's old firm; he learns she's been hired to plan the celebratory gala. He says nothing, telling himself it's strategy. Beat: complicity begins.

chapters.title: Ink and Irony
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Planning the merger gala, she clashes with Daniel in person while falling for Anchor on paper, noting bitterly that both men are stubborn, brilliant, and impossible. Beat: dramatic irony tightens.

chapters.title: What Postcard Didn't Send
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. He drafts a confession revealing his role in destroying Lior's career years ago, then burns it. Instead he sends a letter about his brother's death and the duty that consumed him. Beat: vulnerability traded for concealment.

chapters.title: Venue Scouting, Heart Uncharted
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A site visit strands Lior and Daniel overnight by a storm; forced proximity cracks their hostility into something warmer. That night, both write their correspondents about 'someone I can't forgive.' Beat: enemies softening.

chapters.title: The Mirror Clause
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Her therapist-mandated program essay forces her to confront her own broken engagement — she left at the altar too, not just was left. Beat: the enemy in the mirror named.

chapters.title: Intercepted
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. His business partner discovers the letters and recognizes Lior's voice, threatening exposure unless Daniel kills the merger gala sabotage he'd quietly planned. Beat: blackmail raises stakes.

chapters.title: Postmarked Truth
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A returned envelope reveals the program's address routing — she realizes Anchor writes from Daniel's building. Denial, then dread. Beat: the floor gives way.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Loading Dock
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Lior tests Daniel with a fabricated detail only Anchor would know; he takes the bait. She walks away without telling him she knows. Beat: betrayal crystallizes, revenge plan ignites.

chapters.title: The Sabotage List
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She begins engineering the gala to fail spectacularly — wrong florists, doctored seating chart, a toast designed to humiliate him publicly. Each act feels like armor. Beat: love weaponized.

chapters.title: Letters to No One
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Anchor keeps writing, unaware Postcard has gone silent; his unanswered letters reveal a man dismantling his own defenses. He cancels the partner's sabotage-for-hire scheme. Beat: redemption stirring unseen.

chapters.title: Her Mother's Postcards
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Sorting her late mother's belongings, she finds decades of unsent postcards — her mother's own contained heart, promises never mailed. Beat: generational wound exposed; the price of survival made visible.

chapters.title: Dress Fitting, Confession Fitting
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Gala week. Lior rehearses her destructive toast; Daniel decides to confess everything to Postcard in writing before the event. Their paths cross; almost-tenderness, almost-truth. Beat: tension at maximum pre-climax.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. He mails his final letter — full confession, real name signed — then discovers evidence of Lior's sabotage. He chooses to let the gala proceed anyway, accepting whatever comes. Beat: surrender as courage.

chapters.title: Gala: The Toast
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Mid-gala, she delivers the humiliating toast — but Daniel's confession letter arrives in her hands seconds before, read aloud instead by accident of timing. Public unraveling; guests witness everything. Beat: climax, mutual exposure.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Coat Room
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The same coat room where chapter one began. Rage, then grief, then the raw question: can two people who lied to survive learn to tell the truth? They part without answers. Beat: devastation with a door left open.

chapters.title: Program's End
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Final Bridge Letters session requires reading your correspondent's last letter aloud. She reads his confession to the group, then writes her own — forgiving the person in the mirror. Beat: self-forgiveness achieved.

chapters.title: Unsent, Unsealed
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. He steps down from the merged firm, mailing her mother's recovered postcards back to Lior with one of his own appended: a promise, no conditions. Beat: love offered without leverage.

chapters.title: The Answer
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She finds him at the courthouse where their sentence began, holding a reply she wrote longhand. Not a proposal — a beginning. She tells him the heart isn't a muscle after all; it's a letter you keep choosing to send. Beat: resolution, theme fulfilled.

chapters.title: Postcard and Promise
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. One year later: a tiny wedding planned by no one, witnessed by everyone they hurt and healed. Lior mails her mother's final postcard, finally addressed. Beat: peace; identity rebuilt around truth instead of survival.
